rationale: C09 plausibly supplied a concrete drafting template. Both memoranda disapprove jurisdictional bills involving alleged property damage from a federally constructed dam; both quote machinery overriding limitations and empowering a federal court to “hear, determine, and render judgment”; and both recount flooding-related claims before concluding that ordinary legal finality should not be displaced. The child adapts C09’s limitations-focused dam-claim framework to the stronger circumstance of two prior adverse Court of Claims decisions. C18 and C14 share the child’s repeated-litigation rationale, but lack C09’s unusually close combination of jurisdictional language, dam construction, flooding, and property damage.

shared_material.child_excerpt: notwithstanding any statute of limitation, lapse of time, or any prior court decision ... jurisdiction is hereby conferred upon the United States Court of Claims to hear, determine, and render judgment
shared_material.parent_excerpt: jurisdiction would be vested, notwithstanding any statute of limitations or lapse of time, in the United States District Court ... “to hear, determine, and render judgment”
shared_material.explanation: Distinctive shared jurisdictional formula, with the child adding prior court decisions and changing the court.

shared_material.child_excerpt: damages to its power plant and dam ... sustained as the result of a dam built by the United States
shared_material.parent_excerpt: claims arising as a result of the construction by the United States of Elephant Butte Dam
shared_material.explanation: Both bills concern property-damage claims attributed to construction of a specific federal dam.

shared_material.child_excerpt: the company suffered damages to its facilities from ice jams and flooding in the river
shared_material.parent_excerpt: the severe floods that descended the Rio Grande Valley ... resulted in the permanent seeping or swamping ... of their lands
shared_material.explanation: The same federal-dam-and-flooding factual framework is adapted to a different claimant and water project.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The matters covered by this bill have been fully considered on their merits and decided adversely ... The company has had its day in court
shared_material.parent_excerpt: no showing ... that these landowners did not have an adequate opportunity to pursue their legal remedies within the period prescribed by general law
shared_material.explanation: Both reject special jurisdiction because ordinary judicial remedies and rules already provided an adequate avenue for resolving the claims.
